Are you tired of all your information being scattered?

How many browser tabs do you have open right now?

At **Edvo**, we care deeply about helping people think well. We believe the next revolution in computing will be Personal Intelligence and Intelligence Augmentation — the same way everyone has a personal computer (now multiple personal computers), we have a thesis that everyone will have a personal database that augments them wherever they are, on whichever device they use.

We're starting by helping each of us break out of tab hell, and break into digital spaces designed for thinking and flow.

We're creating the next generation tools for interpersonal computing, to help us make better sense of information and transform passive consumption into active thinking.

This is an end-to-end product design role. You will influence the workflow, prototype the interaction, test the assumptions, define the visual system, and work closely with engineering through implementation.

**About Tegy**
Tegy is building the strategy team ambitious companies wish they had. It turns messy business context into defensible decisions, models, memos, decks, and action plans with senior-grade rigor on demand.

The design opportunity is unusually rich: Tegy must help users bring context into the system, understand how analysis is formed, work with complex outputs, and move from insight to action without making the experience feel like a generic chat interface.

**Why join now**
• Define and continuously improve the core workflows customers rely on.
• Work directly with founders, product, engineering, strategists, and customers.
• Solve a meaningful AI product problem where trust and clarity matter.
• See prototypes move quickly into production and customer use.
• Build the design language and system future product surfaces will inherit.

**What you will own**

2. Information and interaction design. Make complex inputs, system behavior, evidence, assumptions, and outputs understandable without flattening the rigor.
3. Prototyping and validation. Turn uncertain ideas into prototypes, test them with users or strong evidence, and show how the design changed.
4. Product UI and design system. Establish a coherent visual language, components, states, and interaction patterns that can scale with the product.
5. Implementation quality. Work with engineers through build and review so the shipped experience matches the intent and handles real edge cases.

• You collaborate closely with engineers and care about what reaches production.

For sustained, high-ownership engagements, the equity range is 0.0% to 3.0%, with the specific grant shaped by scope, commitment, and demonstrated impact.

This opportunity is open worldwide, with reliable scheduled overlap with US Eastern time for collaboration.

Candidates who advance will shape a focused paid product sprint with clear success outcomes.

Exceptional people rarely arrive on a hiring calendar. We meet strong candidates year-round and move quickly when there is a compelling fit.

## About MyArchitectAI

MyArchitectAI is an AI rendering platform used by architects, interior designers, and visualization professionals in over 150 countries. We turn CAD designs, sketches, and line drawings into photorealistic renders in seconds, with no installs, no hardware requirements, and no learning curve.

We're a team of 5, fully remote, spread across Europe.

## Why we're hiring

Our product works. Our retention and engagement has a lot of room for improvement. Too many people sign up, render a few images, and never come back, or cancel when their current project ends. We have the data (PostHog, Stripe, cancel surveys, live chat) and we have the engineers. What we don't have is one person whose job is to find the leaks and fix them.

That's you.

## What you'll own

**Activation and engagement**
Dig into user behavior in PostHog and Supabase. Figure out where people get stuck between signup and their first "wow" render, and why paying users stop rendering. Turn that into a prioritized list of experiments, run them, and report what moved.

**UX improvements**
Take existing flows and make them simpler and nicer to look at. Our users judge us on how good the app looks, because that's their job. You'll design in Claude Design on top of our existing design system (and improve it), so you do need taste and the ability to tell good from almost good.

**New features from scratch**
From problem to shipped. Talk to users, define the feature, design it, write a spec, QA it on staging, ship it, measure it.

## Who this is for

- You've been a PM, growth PM, or product designer at a SaaS company, ideally one selling to non-technical users. B2B or prosumer both fine.
- You're comfortable doing your own analysis. Funnels, cohorts, SQL, experiment design, knowing when a result is noise.
- You have visual taste and opinions about UI. You can look at a screen and clearly explain why it feels off.
- You write clearly. Most of your output will be specs, hypotheses, and short reports, and other people have to act on them.
- You're self-directed. Nobody will assign you tickets. You'll find the problems yourself.

## Who this is not for

- People who need a designer, an analyst, and an engineer to get anything done.
- People who want to write strategy docs or call all-hands. We need someone who ships fast.

## The deal

- Around 20 hours a week to start. Can grow to full-time if it works for both sides.
- We start with a paid, scoped project so we both see how it goes. If it's good, we move to a monthly retainer.
- You invoice us as a contractor. Location doesn't matter.

## How we work

- Fully remote and mostly async.
- Specs go into Linear. Design happens in Claude Design. Analysis happens in PostHog and SQL.
- We use AI tools heavily and expect you to as well. If you're skeptical of AI-assisted design and coding, this isn't the right place.
- Short feedback loops. You'll get a yes or no within hours, not a week.
- You'll talk to real users. Support is handled by the founders, and you'll have access to every conversation.

## How to apply

Skip the cover letter. Send us:

1. One thing you shipped that moved a metric, and what it moved.
2. Why you're a good fit.
3. Your rate assuming 20hrs/week.

Keep it short. We read everything.

You write the headings and hooks your structure calls for, and our Course Writers and Editors own the final wording. Every course should leave a participant with a portfolio case study they can show a hiring manager.

* **Set and raise the standard for our assessments**, so a correct answer proves understanding, not just recognition, and a good question teaches as well as tests.

* **Make expert knowledge understandable.** You take raw expert video material, course and Master Class transcripts and footage featuring global industry leaders, and turn it into educational material that teaches timeless human-centered design and AI.

### We're Hiring Three People for Our Editorial Team

We're growing, and three roles are open at the same time to build the next generation of our core educational product. Here's what each role leads on:

* **Our Course Directors, UX, UI, and AI**: lead what we teach and who teaches our courses and Master Classes. You reach out to industry leaders and create the invitation they say yes to. You bring your judgment to a planned course outline: what's missing, what doesn't belong, and whether the structure is solid. You plan and shoot courses with our Education Designers **This is the role described here.**

* **[Our Education Designers, UX, UI, and AI](https://ixdf.org/about/careers/education-designer-ux-ui-and-ai)**: lead how design and AI are taught. You plan, structure, and create the core content, and you decide what a course participant should be able to do by the end and how they get there.

* **[Our Course Writers and Editors](https://ixdf.org/about/careers/course-writer-and-editor-ux-ui-and-ai)**: lead how our courses and articles read. You make each title engaging, ensure each sentence flows, and edit the written course experience from the user’s perspective.

We’re a flexible team, and you’ll be able to do what you excel in. Everyone on our team creates courses, and everyone works across these roles. If you're torn between two roles, apply for the one you'd be best at, and tell us in your application which other one you considered and why.

**You, the Course Director**, decide what belongs in our curriculum and who should teach it. You reach out to the world’s leading experts, plan the courses with them, and shoot courses with them. When an Education Designer brings you a course outline, you're the one who says what's missing, what doesn't belong, and how to optimize the learning outcome so designers can succeed today. You'll work closely with our **Co-Founder, your Team Lead, our other Course Directors, and the Education Designers**, and you'll plan and create courses alongside them. Our Course Writers and Editors take the finished material the last mile: the scripts, hooks, headings, on-screen text in videos, quiz wording, and editorial voice. You'll also work closely with the video team and our growth team.

### Your Role at IxDF
* **Be a core part of our Editorial Team.** You'll collaborate with IxDF editors, video editors, and UX and UI designers as well as external industry leaders to create courses and Master Classes for people worldwide. You'll help them succeed in the age of AI with new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design.

* You'll research what already exists in a topic area, so that what we build is genuinely unique. You'll look at **where design and AI are heading, what designers need** that nobody has taught well yet, and **what we should retire** because the field has already moved on.

* **Find the people who should teach it.** You decide a topic is worth a course, you work out who should teach it and why, you write the email, and you get the yes. Then you plan the content with the industry leader and agree what the course must leave a learner able to do.

* **Decide what each expert should teach.** The best designers know a great deal, and a course that tries to capture all of it becomes an information dump. You develop a point of view on what a designer genuinely needs from them, and you hold the course to it.

* **You'll decide which skills our courses teach,** both to people entering design and to experienced designers leveling up. Our goal is to help designers thrive in the age of AI and work responsibly, so their users can thrive too.

* Ensure our course participants finish each course with a solid portfolio project they can show a hiring manager.

* **Help us decide what AI should do for our course participants.** Personalized learning paths, constructive AI feedback on portfolio work, practice environments where people run real design tasks and get feedback. You'll also help us improve the user flows on our own platform, so that learning at IxDF is as well designed as what we teach. You'll work on this with our founders, designers, and dev team.

* **Make an impact as you pressure-test the courses** our Education Designers plan. An Education Designer sends you a course outline, and you read it against everything you know about the field and about how people learn design, then give constructive feedback on what's missing, what doesn't belong, and where the structure can be improved. **You know the limits of your own expertise,** and you research your way past them before you weigh in. You'll also plan, structure, and create courses yourself, alongside them.

* You're one of the people **whose judgment the rest of the team leans on**. You show our Education Designers what ten or twenty years in the field taught you to look for. In return, our Co-Founder, your Team Lead, and our other Course Directors give constructive feedback on the courses you lead. You'll work in a **diverse, highly organized, result-driven environment** where you'll grow personally and professionally.

* **Act as guardian of our quality bar**. When a course goes out under our name, it has to be better than anything else available on the topic. On the courses and Master Classes you lead or review, you're the one who spots what's not good enough yet and works with the team to fix it.

* **Bring your subject matter expertise** to our writers, community managers, and social media team, so our design thinking stays consistent across everything we publish.

* **You help produce Master Classes.** We produce 3 per month. Over email, you reach out to designers whose work you admire, invite them to create one with us, plan the content, and produce the live session. **Timelines vary enormously:** with Don Norman or Vitaly Friedman it can be two weeks from first email to publication, because we work with them often. With a new expert, it can be half a year. Once the session is recorded, you get the footage and the transcript, and you decide with the Education Designers and Team Lead which existing course benefits from which snippets, and where they go.

* **Focus on what matters** as you take raw expert video material, course and Master Class transcripts and footage featuring global industry leaders, and turn it into educational material that teaches new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design. You'll work across UX design, human-computer interaction, design thinking, UI design, psychology, and AI.

* **Design for a diverse, global audience.** Some of our courses and Master Classes serve working designers who want to grow into more senior work. Others serve people moving into design from other fields. Often, a course will serve both in the same lesson. Getting both right without watering either down is a rewarding design challenge.

* Give the video team **constructive feedback** on course and Master Class videos, from on-screen text and b-roll to graphics and animation, so each video is engaging to learn from and accurate from a design perspective.

* **Fly out and meet the global industry leaders in design in professional studios across the world.** You'll shoot the course content there with some of your colleagues. Expect this a few times a year at minimum. Some of us love that part and join every studio production; others keep it to those few trips. Both work for us. On average **we shoot 4-6 new courses per year.**

* Expect to have several courses moving at once at different stages: one you're planning with an expert, one being shot, one in production, and one published course that you're reviewing and improving.

* **Find room for improvement** by looking at completion rates, learner feedback, and the portfolios course participants produce, then go back and fix what isn't excellent yet. Use the power of incremental, modular design as you help push the quality of our educational materials to new heights, surpassing even the very best in industry and academia. We're always learning, always improving, always raising the bar in everything we do and ship.

* Maintain and improve our **crystal-clear documentation** so our knowledge resources stay up-to-date, easy to find, and provide instant value to our internal teams. Clarity is key. Any line of documentation should be self-explanatory.

* We're proud to have assembled a **remarkable team of unicorns** who uplift, motivate, and push each other to excel daily. There's a seat open for someone who shares our passion for excellence. Could that be you?

* You have a **network among designers you respect, and you're comfortable writing to someone you admire** and presenting them with an opportunity.

* You know what the design community wants to see, and what it needs to learn.

* **You can show us something you built or led:** a product, a design team, a course, an AI teaching app, or a conference track. We're excited to hear what it was, your thinking behind it, how long it took you to create, what went wrong, and how you improved it.

* You can take a **broad, complex design practice and turn it into a step-by-step learning sequence** that'll make a beginner feel and act confident. You can look at a plan for teaching something and **see what's missing before anyone builds it.**

* You're a **practical idealist.** You know how to create great results through incremental quick wins and MVPs, and you know when to go all in and make something perfect.

* You’re a **forward thinker** who isn’t afraid to innovate and try new things before others have.

* You’re **eager to help people build UX and UI skills** because you know they’re more relevant than ever in the age of AI.

* You can **teach a career changer** the powerful skills of great design, and you can **guide an experienced designer** in upskilling. Perhaps you've mentored people, or you’ve run your own company helping clients level up.

* You **give constructive feedback people can act on**, and you can tell a talented colleague how they can improve their work without them becoming defensive.

* You're genuinely **curious** about how AI is changing design work and design education.

* You're **fluent in written and spoken English** and you can explain complex ideas clearly.

* You’re enthusiastic about learning by doing and are **committed to putting in the effort to continuously improve your skills.**

* You **spot problems** before anyone else notices them, and when something goes off track you come back with a solution rather than a report.

* You **value teamwork**, prioritize collaboration, and focus on collective goals and harmony in the workplace.

* You're **self-motivated**, and you love **creative freedom, independent judgment**, and the **responsibility** that comes with both.

* You’re driven by the desire to **make a positive impact in the world** and to improve the lives of others.

**ABOUT LENOX PARK SOLUTIONS**

Lenox Park Solutions’ mission is to use collaborative technology and data science to democratize opportunity access, primarily in the financial services industry.
Lenox Park Solutions is an early-stage FinTech company developing innovative tools and resources to enhance collaboration and data-driven decision-making for investors and financial professionals. With a strong foundation in investment banking and asset management, the company has honed technological best practices through partnerships with some of the world’s most respected investment firms.
At the core of Lenox Park Solutions’ offerings is ‘RoundTables’, an exclusive, cloud-based data platform, which enables organizations to efficiently and securely gather and centralize relevant metrics and data. This allows decision makers to measure ‘Impact’ to inform and assess investment decisions. Lenox Park Solutions has successfully introduced its technology to the marketplace, attracting a prestigious client base that includes some of the most sophisticated and globally well-respected investment institutions.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

We are seeking a fractional UX/UI DESIGN PARTNER (an independent designer or a small design firm) to bring dedicated design attention to RoundTables, Lenox Park Solutions’ platform. The engagement reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and works in close, hands-on collaboration with the engineering team, the Product Manager, and the client services team; the colleagues on the front lines with the platform’s day-to-day users and with the clients who rely on RoundTables for reporting and survey administration. This is the company’s first dedicated design role: to date, design has been handled in-house only informally, by team members whose primary responsibilities lay elsewhere, and bringing in focused design expertise is a deliberate next step for a maturing platform.
Lenox Park Solutions has invested substantially in RoundTables including professional design work delivered through a previous external design engagement and the platform already serves a sophisticated client base. This is not a rebuild or a redesign from scratch; it is an opportunity to take strong, established work and make it better for the people who use it. The focus is on enhancing the experience of current users: bringing greater consistency to the design, refining the most important workflows, and closing the gap between design intent and what reaches production. A core part of the engagement is developing a deep understanding of the user journey which may include research with Lenox Park’s clients and the asset owners, asset managers, and survey administrators who use RoundTables ensuring design decisions are grounded in real use.

**RESPONSIBILITIES & QUALIFICATIONS**

As Lenox Park Solutions’ UX/UI Design Partner you will:

1. Work with the platform as it exists today and make it clearer, more consistent, and easier to use.
2. Develop a deep understanding of the RoundTables user journey including, where useful, research with clients and end users, and apply it to refine the platform’s most important experiences, such as the dashboards and workflows used by survey hosts, survey takers, and administrators, the survey-taking experience, the manager impact report, and contact-list management.
3. Bring consistency to the platform’s existing design language, establishing clear, brand-aligned standards and reusable patterns in Figma so design and engineering stay aligned and new work ships faithfully.
4. Collaborate closely and iteratively with the engineering team, the Product Manager, and the client services team, producing development-ready specifications and handoff documentation so that what reaches production matches what was designed.

The ideal designer or firm brings:

1. Demonstrated experience designing and shipping B2B SaaS or data-platform interfaces, ideally complex, data-dense web applications, supported by a portfolio of end-to-end UX and UI work.
2. A strong UX foundation in user research, role-based information architecture, and user-journey mapping, with the ability to translate how a product is actually used into clear, prioritized design improvements.
3. Proven skill in working within an existing product, refining and enhancing live interfaces and bringing consistency to an established design language, rather than rebuilding from the ground up.
4. Fluency with Figma for design standards, reusable components, and accessible, WCAG-aligned patterns, alongside a rigorous, developer-ready handoff practice that keeps production output faithful to the agreed design.
5. A self-directed, collaborative operating style suited to a fractional, milestone-based independent engagement, and comfort working hands-on alongside an internal engineering, product, and client services team.

**COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS**

This is a fractional, independent-contractor engagement rather than a salaried employee position, and compensation is milestone-based rather than hourly. Each phase of work, from user-journey research through refined platform workflows, design standards, and developer handoff, is tied to a defined deliverable and a fixed fee agreed in advance, so investment is predictable and linked directly to completed outcomes.
• Independent-contractor (1099) engagement; open to either an individual designer or a design firm.
• Compensation structured as fixed fees tied to agreed project milestones and deliverables, rather than hourly billing.
• Milestones, deliverables, and fees defined and scheduled with the selected designer or firm before work begins, with payment on acceptance of each completed milestone.
• A fractional, project-scoped engagement, with the possibility of an ongoing design retainer once the initial milestones are complete.

**BENEFITS**

As an independent-contractor engagement, this role is not eligible for the employee benefits programs offered to Lenox Park Solutions’ US-based staff which include medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, health and wellness reimbursement, and a 401(k) plan.

**LOCATION**

Remote. Lenox Park Solutions’ staff work remotely, as we believe team members are most productive when they live in the places they choose and establish schedules that offer flexibility. Certain meetings may take place in person and require physical presence in New York City.

**COME WORK WITH US!**

If this opportunity sounds appealing to you, please email a resume and a portfolio — or, for firms, representative case studies — to lps.careers1@lenoxparkinc.com. A brief note describing relevant SaaS or data-platform design work and your approach to design systems is encouraged but optional.

**DEADLINE TO APPLY: **Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

**OPTIMIZING HUMAN CAPITAL**

At Lenox Park, we measure diversity rather than describe it. We built the Lenox Park Impact Score (LPI), in collaboration with our clients, to benchmark human capital optimization across ownership, leadership, and workforce on both gender and racial/ethnic dimensions, and we hold our own firm to the standard we set for everyone else. In an industry not known for representation, the numbers speak plainly: Lenox Park ranks in the 94th percentile of 3,249 asset management firms on the RoundTables platform overall, and in the 95th percentile for racial representation across our workforce. We are equally committed to building an environment where colleagues who identify as LGBTQIA+, as neurodivergent, or as religious minorities feel genuinely welcomed and where gender representation, in the 74th percentile of firms on the platform, keeps improving as we grow. If you want to do excellent work somewhere that measures what it claims to value and holds itself to it, you’ll be in good company here.

**OUR HOPE**

We continue to assemble exceptionally talented and diverse individuals, so our firm has the best chance of maintaining the trajectory of success we have established to date. Individuals who have found the most comprehensive forms of success and fulfillment at Lenox Park Solutions tend to align with our mission. They also exhibit professionalism, natural curiosity about the finance or technology arenas, and an eagerness to learn. We value individuals who have a record of great judgement and a keen interest in developing themselves and the team around them. We are driven by a mission that prioritizes representation and opportunity. We hold ourselves accountable to setting an example, and being the change we want to see in the world.

Casino & Sportsbook UI/UX Designer

Share

Post

Copy

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a hands-on Product UI/UX Designer to shape the player-facing experience of a B2C casino and sportsbook across desktop and mobile web. This is a long-term product design role—not front-end development, slot-game illustration, or banner-only production.

CREATIVITY IS THE CORE OF THIS ROLE

We need someone who can originate distinctive visual concepts, not simply rearrange templates. You should be able to take a product brief, explore multiple directions, explain your decisions, and turn the strongest idea into a cohesive, intuitive interface.

Our design direction is clean, premium, familiar, and comfortable to use. We value thoughtful typography, spacing, hierarchy, reusable components, subtle motion, and strong attention to detail. The product includes Korean-language layouts, but Korean fluency is not required.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Propose original visual directions and interaction ideas that give the product a recognizable identity.

• Design responsive homepages, casino lobbies, game cards, search, filters, promotions, and navigation.

• Design sportsbook event lists, odds displays, markets, live states, and bet-slip interactions.

• Improve sign-up, account, wallet, transaction history, notifications, messages, and promotion screens.

• Turn user flows into polished screens, interactive prototypes, and reusable Figma components.

• Define desktop/mobile behavior and hover, focus, selected, disabled, loading, empty, and error states.

• Collaborate with the product owner and developers on implementation details and visual QA.

• Occasionally support promotional banners and lightweight UI motion; product UI remains the primary focus.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

• Strong creative judgment and a portfolio showing original concepts, exploration, and polished execution.

• 2+ years of hands-on web or product UI/UX design experience.

• At least one relevant casino OR sportsbook website project; experience in both is a plus.

• Strong Figma skills: Auto Layout, components, variants, variables/styles, prototypes, and organized developer handoff.

• Solid responsive design, typography, information hierarchy, and interaction design skills.

• Working English for written communication and design discussions.

• Ability to explain exactly what you personally owned and why you made key design decisions.

NICE TO HAVE

• Experience with Korean or other Asian-market consumer interfaces.

• Design systems for content-rich products.

• Micro-interaction prototypes, subtle motion, or promotional banner design.

• Basic understanding of HTML/CSS constraints; coding is not required.

ENGAGEMENT

• Long-term, fully remote contract with full-time-equivalent availability.

• Monthly compensation: USD 1,500–2,000, depending on portfolio quality and relevant experience.

• Candidates worldwide are welcome; working-hour overlap can be discussed.

• Shortlisted candidates may be invited to a small paid trial before the long-term engagement.

HOW TO APPLY

Share 1–3 relevant projects and briefly explain:

1. Which screens, components, and design decisions you personally owned.

2. One original idea you introduced, the alternatives you explored, and why you chose the final direction.

3. Your experience with casino lobbies, sportsbook odds/markets, bet slips, wallets, or other relevant flows.

4. Your availability and expected monthly compensation.

Desktop/mobile examples and an NDA-safe Figma walkthrough are welcome. AI-assisted work is acceptable, but you must demonstrate your own design decisions and editable, production-ready work. Generic templates, banner-only portfolios, and AI-generated screenshots alone are not sufficient.

Designer

Design Design the Future of Commerce

Shopify’s mission is to make commerce better for everyone. We wake up every day focused on ways to inspire, enable, and support entrepreneurs. We are transforming how millions of unique brands start, run, and grow their businesses - and we are just getting started.

Design has always been essential to this mission. It is our DNA—defining how we build products, solve problems, grow the company, empower our merchants, and engage their buyers.

Who we’re looking for

We are always looking for tasteful designers who move fast, sweat details, are technically fluent, and love to tinker. Entrepreneurial energy drives our mission and our internal culture. We want designers that are prolific and prefer less process and more freedom to build. We want designers that break boundaries between product and brand, art and technology, imagery and words. We are a fully remote company so we need people that speak up, share openly, and are proactive in creating connections. Most importantly we want people that are courageous and curious - in their work, in their giving and sharing feedback, and in their appetite to embrace the new, the difficult and the unknown.

AI? Ok, let’s talk about it.

Yes, AI is changing everything. And yes, we’re all in.

We are embracing AI in our tools, workflows and philosophies because we believe technology will always create opportunities for those sufficiently courageous to claim it. We want people committed to the tools of tomorrow, because true innovation happens when craft excellence meets technological audacity. We are confident that in a world where AI can help produce almost anything, designers that can master and wield these tools with incredible taste and judgement are even more necessary than ever.

Want to hear more about Shopify and AI? Get it straight from the top.

This is where you come in

Here’s what we expect from designers at Shopify:

You are an opinionated tastemaker

You are a connoisseur of software design and digital culture and can confidently push its boundaries.

You are a master of your craft

You wield rock-solid design fundamentals and have an obsession for detail and a deep appreciation for craft.

You’re a hands-on builder, coach and student

You revel in making things, trying things, sharing things and taking ownership of your own development.

You are driven

You thrive in and help create an uptempo environment, generating a lot of ideas, showing your work often, shipping fast, and always pushing to get your project to the next step. You raise the energy on teams around you, and elevate your teammates by showing them what is possible.

You embrace new tools

You grab hold of every new tool as soon as you can, and fearlessly push the edges of what is possible.

You are technically fluent

You’re comfortable working close to the code, proactively collaborate with engineers, and are comfortable prototyping your work directly.

Most importantly, you care

Good design work comes from craft excellence, and we certainly expect that of you. But great design work comes from care. You care deeply about our mission, our merchants, and the world we want to serve. A spirit of care is what comes through is our unreasonable attention to every detail, every word, every millisecond of performance, every support interaction. It is care that animates our brand. If care and working on something meaningful is what drives you to strive and wield your skills and tools expertly…then Shopify might be for you.

About Shopify

Opportunity is not evenly distributed. Shopify puts independence within reach for anyone with a dream to start a business. We propel entrepreneurs and enterprises to scale the heights of their potential. Since 2006, we’ve grown to over 8,300 employees and generated over $1 trillion in sales for millions of merchants in 175 countries.

This is life-defining work that directly impacts people’s lives as much as it transforms your own. This is putting the power of the few in the hands of the many, is a future with more voices rather than fewer, and is creating more choices instead of an elite option.

If you believe entrepreneurship can change lives, and you want your work to fuel that change, let us know.

Design for JTX across web and mobile, including order entry, market data, charts, positions, execution visibility, onboarding, and wallet flows.

Take features from defining the problem through UX and final UI.

Strong product sense: you can explain why a decision is right, not just that it looks good.

Trading terminals, exchange or brokerage products.

Consumer fintech apps at scale.

Data-dense or real-time interfaces, such as dashboards, analytics, or live data visualization.

Self-custodial wallets, Solana or EVM products.

Experience building or maintaining a token-based design system.

As our new Senior Product Designer , you'll lead and execute product initiatives from concept to UI, bringing a user-focused mentality to everything you ship. •

Own design projects end to end (concept, scoping, user flows, UI, release, and follow-up), at any scale, from small improvements to strategic new capabilities.

•

Drive discovery: define what to build to address real problems and user needs, and study competitors and best practices.

•

Work closely with Research, Product Management, and Development: request and apply insights, align on business requirements, and validate technical feasibility.

•

Write clear specifications so design intent is unambiguous, and run design QA against both the intent and the Kinsta Design System.

•

Give clear rationale for your decisions, resolve design and product deadlocks, escalate when you need feedback or mediation, and communicate trade-offs when priorities compete.

•

Serve as Project Owner on occasion. We don't have full-time delivery managers, so one team member leads each project as its Owner during delivery, communicating progress and coordinating releases.

•

Be a product expert: know how our product works, the personas and use cases we support, and how that translates into UI-level design solutions.

Represent the craft: uphold professional standards in design thinking, problem solving, usability, UX, and UI; give and receive design critique; and help maintain and evolve the Kinsta Design System.

•

A minimum of 5 years of hands-on experience as a Product or UX Designer.

•

Demonstrated experience shipping products and features from zero to production, with the ability to carry a project fully autonomously.

•

Experience working in a SaaS product environment.

•

Hands-on experience across the full design workflow: research, problem definition, ideation and facilitation, creating UI, and partnering in delivery.

•

Expert-level proficiency with Figma.

•

Experience working with and maintaining a design system.

•

A portfolio with at least one case study taking a project from a problem statement to a delivered solution. We want to see your process and how you arrived at decisions, not only screens and a general workflow description.

•

A good understanding of front-end technologies (HTML, CSS, JS). You don't need to write production code, but you should have a working sense of feasibility and be comfortable poking at things in an Inspector.

•

Proactivity: you take the initiative rather than waiting to be told what to do.

•

Professional-level English with excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Bonus if you have:

•

Experience working on a hosting or web infrastructure product.

•

Experience with technical products where the audience is developers or technology-oriented users.

•

Experience with the WordPress ecosystem.

Annual remote expense budget.

Flexible PTO.

Paid parental leave.

Location-specific healthcare benefits (includes vision and dental) for employees hired in the USA, UK, Canada, and Hungary.

Pension plan for employees hired in the UK, and 401k contributions for employees hired in the USA.

About CutTime

CutTime is a fine arts management platform that empowers fine arts educators, administrators, and boosters to run their programs more efficiently, freeing up more time for teaching. Our customers rely on CutTime to help them manage all of the administrative overhead of running a fine arts program like communicating with families, keeping track of instruments and uniforms, collecting payments, and more.

www.gocuttime.com

About the role

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer with sharp product thinking, strong design fundamentals, and an ability to own projects from concept to delivery.

What you’ll do

•
Lead research and design projects end-to-end.

•
Partner closely with engineering and product to complete projects on the roadmap.

•
Create mockups, prototypes, and high-fidelity visuals to communicate your ideas and describe their intent and execution.

•
Lead user research and report your findings to help us make better decisions.

•
Mentor and collaborate with our associate researcher on research projects.

•
Use and improve our design system.

•
Review built features to ensure they match design intent and quality standards.

•
Participate in our hiring process as we grow the team.

What we’re looking for

Required

•
3-4 hour overlap with US Pacific Time

•
5+ years experience designing software

•
Strong interaction and visual design fundamentals

•
Experience with prototyping (we’re currently using Figma, Claude Code, and Codex/ChatGPT primarily, but we encourage you to explore new tooling and share your learnings with the team)

•
Experience leading user research

•
Experience mentoring others or leading teams

•
Excellent written and verbal communication skills (in fluent, though not necessarily native, English)

Nice-to-have

•
Experience designing complex admin tooling: permissions, multiple role types, records management, financial workflows, or reporting.

•
Experience designing for education or non-profits

•
Experience building and maintaining design systems

•
Expertise or interest in accessibility

•
Familiarity with basic HTML, CSS, and component architecture

If you don’t meet all the requirements above, we encourage you to apply anyway. We’re most interested in hiring capable, kind, deep thinkers who want autonomy and ownership in their next role. Relevant experience helps, but we know the best candidates can come from varied backgrounds. We want to hear how your past work aligns with the work you’ll be doing at CutTime.

What it’s like to work with us

CutTime is a small and mighty company, and we know how to do a lot with a little. You’ll be the first design hire reporting directly to our Head of UX and collaborating closely with 4-5 engineers, our Head of Engineering, and our product manager. While we care a lot about our customers, we put our team first.

•
You’ll have the support you need balanced with the autonomy to structure your work in a way that best suits you.

•
You’ll be part of a collaborative and engaged cross-functional team. While our design team is small, you’ll have plenty of people around you to sharpen your thinking, provide feedback, and pair on problems.

•
We value focused work. Most of your time will be spent doing research and design.

•
As a team, we value accountability over availability while staying highly collaborative. We often use Slack, Gather, Linear, and Loom to communicate our ideas async without expecting responses immediately.

•
Each week, you’ll participate in a research standup and a 1:1 with our Head of UX, but we’ll leave it up to you to decide what other meetings you need to move work forward.

•
We care about a healthy work-life balance. You won’t be working more than 40 hours a week except during the rarest of emergencies.

•
Work stays at work. We don’t expect you to have Slack on your phone or answer email during your off hours.

What we offer

For full-time employees based in the United States:

•
Salary range: $140k-150k depending on experience

•
3 weeks paid vacation, plus 13 paid holidays

•
$4,000 annual office stipend

•
Health coverage through an HRA

•
Basic life and short-term disability insurance

•
401(k) with company match

•
Remote-first with no required commute

Our hiring process

Our hiring process is designed to give us the best sense of who you are, your relevant past experience, and how you think through problems without being overly demanding of your time. We know interviewing can be a stressful, long process, so we don’t require white boarding, take-home assignments, or all-day on-site interviews.

1. Application

You submit your resume and portfolio and fill out a short questionnaire. Our team reviews each one and will reach out if you’re selected for the next round.

2. Non-technical interview (30 min)

If we choose to move forward, we’ll follow up with a 30-minute non-technical call where we can learn about your background, what you’re looking for, and whether the role may be a good fit for both sides.

3. Past work presentation (45 min)

You’ll present some of your past work with a focus on your design process, how you solve problems and overcome challenges, and how you communicate and collaborate with a cross-functional team. We would like to see something beyond just a walk through of your portfolio, ideally a presentation deck with 1-2 polished case studies.

4. App critique (30 min)

We’ll ask you to critique an app to get a sense of how you think about product, systems, and visual craft, as well as how you prioritize and communicate. At the start of the interview, we’ll provide you with a Figma file containing a flow from an app we’ve selected and ask you to share your screen during the critique.

5. Decision and offer

Our team will review your materials and scores from each interview round. If you’re selected, we’ll extend an offer, discuss logistics, and give you time to decide.

Diversity and inclusion

Description

Position at ARRISE

ABOUT THE ROLE
We are building out our design capability for the tools that power our business from the inside out — platform, live casino, and studio operations, as well as the tools our operator partners use directly. This isn't about designing for players. It's about designing for scale. When thousands of people rely on the same workflow every single day, a small improvement — shaving a few clicks off a repetitive task, clarifying a confusing status flow — adds up to a massive impact across the business. If you love the kind of design work where the ROI is measurable and the problems are real, this is that role. A well-designed workflow here doesn't just look good; it removes friction at scale. Small improvements compound fast when they're used constantly, by many people, every single day. You'll work across platform, live casino, and studio tooling depending on the project, partnering closely with product, engineering, and a design team that spans Europe and India. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING
• Own the design of internal and operator-facing tools end to end — from a vague problem statement through to delivery-ready specs.

• Take ambiguous, undefined business problems and turn them into clear design direction — often with no existing brief or precedent to lean on.

• Spot when a problem isn't a one-off — and build systemic solutions instead of patching the same issue over and over.

• Set your own success metrics. Track task time, usage, and adoption, and let real data — not opinion — drive your decisions.

• Build and scale a design system that grows with a widening product surface.

• Present your thinking regularly to stakeholders and defend your rationale under real scrutiny.

• Work directly with the engineers and PMs who bring your designs to life.

• Help shape direction for other designers touching the same products — no formal authority required, just clear thinking and good instincts.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
Communication is critical to this role. You'll be presenting, aligning, and defending design thinking on a near-daily basis — with product, engineering, operations stakeholders, and fellow designers. We're looking for someone who can:
• Communicate clearly and concisely, with a defined point and structure — not open-ended or rambling

• Respond to challenge or new information with openness and adaptability, not defensiveness

• Manage stakeholders and cross-functional relationships independently, without needing a hand held — with the executive presence to be trusted in the room.

Beyond communication, you'll bring:
• Systems and workflow thinking — You naturally zoom out from a single screen to the workflow it's part of — and design for scale, not just for the task in front of you.

• UX-led craft. You don't need to be the sharpest visual designer in the room, but you do need real UX instincts: setting KPIs, reading usage data, letting behavior — not assumption — guide your decisions. Solid UI and design-system fluency are a given.

• A high tolerance for ambiguity. No brief? No problem. You can define the problem yourself, scope it, and get moving — this matters more here than in almost any other design role.

• Genuine curiosity. A real drive to make things better, not just familiarity with tools — Figma is a given, and openness to new tools (including AI-assisted workflows) is a good signal of that mindset, but the curiosity itself is what we're after. We want people with opinions, not just preferences.

** Prior iGaming experience is not required , and we're actively encouraging designers without it to apply. We're especially interested in candidates from B2B or SaaS environments, where working directly with business customers — and navigating ambiguity without a pre-defined brief — tends to be the norm rather than the exception. We're not looking for someone who checks every box perfectly. We're looking for someone strong and well-rounded across all of the above, with communication and ambiguity tolerance as the areas we weight most heavily.

ABOUT ARRISE
ARRISE sets the benchmark for service delivery and excellence in the iGaming industry. Playing a key role in the success of its clients, ARRISE helps to deliver exceptional gaming experiences to millions of players worldwide. 
Our global team of over 11,000 talented and driven professionals are shaping the future of iGaming. Headquartered in Gibraltar, we have offices spanning Canada, India, the Isle of Man, Latvia, Malta, Romania, Serbia, Bulgaria, and the UAE, and more exciting destinations on the horizon. 
At ARRISE, we take pride in creating growth opportunities at all levels, constantly investing in our people while welcoming new colleagues and forging strategic partnerships that open new opportunities for success.  To achieve this, we bet on ourselves. We know that success is a collective effort, and our team is driven by ambition, collaboration, and a shared commitment to grow and succeed — while embracing every step of the journey.

You not only have a high bar for visual craft, but you understand how a user moves through the experience. What You'll Do:

• Own the Journey: Design and improve key growth surfaces like landing pages, onboarding, pricing, checkout, and upgrade flows

• Connect the Experience: Make the end-to-end journey feel seamless across marketing and in-product touchpoints

• Lead GTM Design: Support go-to-market efforts across the website, lifecycle (email, in-app), and feature launches

• Drive Experimentation: Work with Product and Growth to shape hypotheses, run A/B tests, and iterate based on what you learn

• Prototype to Learn: Quickly bring ideas to life to test, validate, and move faster with more confidence

• Improve Conversion: Use data and research to spot friction, refine flows, and move key metrics

• Raise the Bar: Push the quality of visual, interaction, and motion design across everything you touch

What You Will Bring to Coupa:

• 5+ years of Product-Led Growth Experience: You understand how funnels, conversion, and experimentation actually play out in real products and drive business impact.

• Journey Thinking: You naturally think in flows and systems, with a focus on time to first value.

• Narrative Instinct: You can simplify complex ideas and carry a clear narrative across different touchpoints.

• High Craft: You care about the details and it shows in your visual and interaction design work. You have experience with brand and product packaging.

• Comfort with Experimentation: You’ve worked on A/B tests and know how to design for iteration, not perfection.

• Fast Prototyping: Skilled at bringing ideas to life quickly with modern design tools.

• Data-Aware: You use data and research to guide decisions, without getting stuck in it

• Easy to Work With: You collaborate well with Product, Marketing, and Engineering and can adapt as things change.

What Success Looks Like:

• First 3 Months: You build a deep understanding of our users, funnel, and growth levers. You identify friction points and begin shaping early experiments. You establish trust with cross-functional partners and start contributing to meaningful improvements in key flows.

• By 6 Months: You are driving multiple experiments end-to-end, with clear hypotheses and measurable outcomes. You’ve improved critical conversion points (e.g., onboarding, pricing, checkout) and delivered cohesive GTM experiences that connect marketing and product more seamlessly.

• By 12 Months: You are a key driver of growth strategy through design. The experiences you’ve shaped measurably improve activation, conversion, and retention. You’ve helped establish a more unified journey across all touchpoints and raised the bar for how design contributes to business impact.

We are seeking a product designer to architect the comprehensive user experience for Objection’s media claims dispute resolution platform. The interface must guide users through complex adversarial adjudication processes with confidence, clarity, and institutional trust — and the designer must build it with AI-native tools and workflows from the ground up.

This is not a conventional UX role. You will translate intricate procedural workflows and legalistic frameworks into seamless, frictionless digital interactions. You will minimize cognitive load for users engaging with a system designed to resolve disputes through structured argumentation, evidence evaluation, and AI-assisted adjudication.

This role is suited for professionals accustomed to:

•
Designing for complex, high-stakes, process-heavy products where clarity is non-negotiable

•
Transforming dense procedural or legal logic into intuitive user flows

•
Using AI tooling and agentic workflows to accelerate and augment design output

•
Working autonomously with structured written communication in distributed teams

The Role

As an Agentic Product Designer, you will:

•
Design the end-to-end user experience for Objection’s adversarial adjudication platform — from claim submission through tribunal output

•
Transform complex procedural workflows into seamless, frictionless digital interactions that minimize cognitive load

•
Establish a premium, high-trust visual language that reflects the institutional gravity of the platform

•
Develop and maintain a robust, scalable design system that ensures consistency across the entire product and accelerates development velocity

•
Conduct rigorous user research and usability testing to iterate on designs and solve real-world friction points

•
Partner closely with engineering and product management to ensure design fidelity is maintained from prototype to production

•
Embed inclusive design principles into the core of the product, ensuring the platform is universally accessible and equitable

•
Leverage AI-native design tools and agentic workflows to increase output, accelerate iteration, and systematize design operations

Who You Are

Required Experience

Professional product design experience with a strong portfolio in complex, data-rich, or process-heavy digital products. Demonstrated ability to take a product’s UX from architecture through to production-ready design.

Core Competencies

•
Deep empathy for the user, combined with the ability to impose clarity on complex systems

•
Precision in UI craft — you approach visual design with the rigor of an engineer and the sensibility of an artist

•
Systems thinking — you design for scalability, edge cases, and procedural integrity, not just the happy path

•
Fluency with AI-native design tools and a bias toward automating and systematizing design workflows

•
Comfort working autonomously in a distributed, asynchronous environment with clear written output

•
Experience pairing with developers to ensure implementation fidelity

•
Strong commitment to accessibility and inclusive design

A background in legal, fintech, govtech, or other high-trust, process-heavy domains is a strong advantage — but design instinct and rigor matter more than sector tenure.

Not a brand-only or marketing design role

Not wireframing to someone else’s specification

Not visual polish applied after the product is built

Not a role where AI tooling is optional

This is designing the environment in which truth is adjudicated. The UX is the product. And the designer builds with AI, not around it.

Round-trip flights, hotel accommodation, and structured summit programming provided

Meaningful equity grants and annual performance bonus

We will calibrate seniority and scope to the right candidate

You'll be designing the future of product discovery: the moment a shopper goes from intent to purchase, reimagined through AI.

• Visual strategy — Defining a bold design direction that represents what product discovery looks like in 2027.

• High-fidelity delivery — Producing final mockups and assets across key surfaces: homepage, search, PDP, filtering, guided shopping, and agent configuration.

• UX patterns — Ensuring designs scale within Constructor's evolving design system and component library.

TIME Magazine named Goodbill one of the Best Inventions of 2023 , highlighting our ability to flag unnecessary services and negotiate waste out of hospital bills. Since then, we’ve expanded to serve over 5,000 employers and 250,000 patients , partnering deeply with TPAs to deliver savings upstream for self-funded plans.

Along the way, we’ve earned accolades like the BBB Spark Award and the Front CSAT Award (2025) for outstanding customer satisfaction, while drawing attention from national press. Backed by top venture firms including Eniac, Maveron, Founders’ Co-op, Reach Capital, and Liquid2 , we’re building the trusted infrastructure to make hospital care cost less.

About the role

We’re hiring a Product Design Lead to own the end-to-end design of everything Goodbill builds: from complex enterprise workflows used by healthcare administrators to simple, delightful consumer experiences that help patients understand and reduce their medical costs.

This is a foundational role. You'll inherit an early-stage Figma component library and transform it into a scalable design system. You'll work directly with our CTO and CEO (who currently serves as the product designer) to establish the design function, raise the bar on every surface of the product, and help shape Goodbill's evolving brand positioning. You'll design for 3–4 engineers shipping up to 20 times a day, which means your work needs to be clear, decisive, and fast enough to keep pace with a team that doesn't wait.

Goodbill sits at a rare intersection: enterprise-grade B2B tools that manage claims, automate financial assistance applications, and route complex workflows, alongside consumer UX that needs to feel as effortless as the best apps. You'll own both, roughly 50/50, and should be thrilled by the range.

We believe the best healthcare software should be the easiest software. Your job is to make complex things feel simple, or at least feel simple at first blush, for claims teams, patients, and everyone in between.

You will:

• Own product design end-to-end. From discovery and customer conversations through wireframes, prototypes, high-fidelity mocks, and production. You're responsible for the full arc. You'll talk to customers daily: joining sales calls, customer syncs, running user research, sitting in on support tickets, whatever it takes to build the right thing.

• Build the design system. Take our nascent Figma component library and turn it into a real system that is consistent, scalable, and opinionated enough to accelerate engineering throughput dramatically.

• Design for AI-native experiences. Rethink traditional healthcare workflows through the lens of what AI makes possible. You're not adding AI to existing patterns; you're designing new patterns that couldn't exist without it.

• Ship to production. Use AI-assisted development tools (we use Devin, but you're welcome to use Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or whatever you prefer) to take your designs from Figma to deployed code, even if incrementally. You'll be empowered and expected to close the gap between design and production yourself.

• Shape brand and positioning . Goodbill's visual identity is always evolving. You'll have a strong voice in where it goes, always ensuring we present a sharper, more intentional expression of who we are and where we're headed.

• Partner deeply with engineering, operations, and leadership. You'll report to our CTO and work closely with our CEO. You'll design alongside 3–4 engineers in a team that moves extremely fast. Your designs need to be clear enough to build from immediately and flexible enough to evolve as we learn.

You are:

• A systems thinker who sweats the pixels. You can hold the entire product in your head while obsessing over a 2px alignment issue. You see how a component decision cascades across five surfaces and you care about all of them.

• Ruthless about killing your darlings. You don't get emotionally attached to your work. You get attached to outcomes. If a better solution emerges, from a customer conversation, an engineer's suggestion, or your own second look, you move to it without ego.

• AI-fluent. You use AI tools daily for prototyping, production, and pixel-perfection. You understand what agentic AI products feel like and you design for them natively, not as an afterthought.

• Fast and decisive. You thrive in environments where speed matters. You know when a rough wireframe is the right artifact and when a polished prototype is worth the time. You default to shipping over perfecting.

• Customer-obsessed. You're not designing from your desk. You're on calls, reading tickets, watching sessions. You build empathy through direct contact, not assumptions.

• Comfortable with complexity. Healthcare is messy: regulatory requirements, EDI standards, insurance jargon, and emotionally-charged moments for patients. You're energized by the challenge of making all of that disappear behind a clean interface.

• A strong communicator. You can articulate design rationale to engineers, executives, and customers with equal clarity. You bring people along without slowing down.

• Collaborative. You’ll work closely with Product, Operations, Sales, and Client Success to design features that move real dollars in the healthcare system.

Bonus

• Experience designing in healthcare, fintech, or other regulated domains.

• Familiarity with healthcare billing, claims processing, or insurance administration.

• You've built or contributed to a design system from the ground up.

• You’ve worked in an early-stage startup (pre-seed/seed/Series A).

• You've shipped code to production using AI-assisted design and development tools.

Why Goodbill

• Massive problem, huge upside. Americans and employers spend nearly half a trillion dollars a year on hospital care — much of it wasted. We’re fixing that with AI and software.

• Recognition + traction. Named one of TIME’s Best Inventions of 2023 ; serving 5,000+ employers and 250,000 patients ; backed by top VCs (Eniac, Maveron, Founders’ Co-op, Reach Capital, Liquid2).

• Rare design range. You'll design enterprise admin tools and consumer experiences in the same week, possibly the same day. Few roles offer this breadth at this stage.

• Ground-floor impact. You're building the design function. Your decisions on systems, patterns, and brand will define Goodbill's product for years.

• Mission-driven team. We live our values: do it for the patient, lead without ego, be transparent, own it, move quickly, sweat the details.

We offer

• Competitive pay (cash and equity)

• Unlimited PTO (Seriously — it’s not an empty benefit. We work too hard for anything else.)

• Health, dental, and vision plans covered 100% for you and 50% for dependents

• A monthly fitness stipend

• Internet or co-working space stipend

• Primary care membership stipend

• Remote office equipment stipend

• Quarterly team retreats

• Establish and evolve a practical design system in Figma

• Define and document reusable components without slowing execution

A Avesdo is hiring Senior UX Designer

TYPE Full Time CATEGORY UX Design LOCATION Remote Anywhere
This job post is over 2 months old and may no longer be available.

The Role

We are looking for a fully remote Senior UX Designer to lead the complete rebuild of our core B2B contracting and administration platform. We are transitioning a legacy system into a modern, performant application using React, Tailwind, and Shadcn UI .

Your challenge is unique: Our users are experts in contracts and administration, not technology. They manage complex, high-stakes workflows, but they need an interface that feels simple, safe, and intuitive. You will bridge the gap between "powerful functionality" and "ease of use."

Why This Role Matters

Contracting and administration are historically dense, paper-heavy processes. You aren't just digitizing a form; you are orchestrating how our customers manage their business relationships. You will define how our "mid-enterprise" clients interact with the platform for the next 5-10 years, moving them from a legacy experience to a modern, component-driven interface.

What you will focus on first

You will lead the early rebuild of our core platform experiences, starting with navigation and information architecture, then moving into data-heavy reporting and inventory-style workflows, then expanding into core objects (people and documents), the transactional workflows that connect those objects, and finally supporting admin surfaces like settings, activity logs, and audit history.

This role is designed for someone who excels in complex B2B SaaS UX and component-based systems.

Key Responsibilities

Simplifying Complexity (The Core Challenge)

• Workflow Distillation: Take complex, multi-stage contracting lifecycles and distill them into linear, understandable user flows for non-technical users.

• Information Density: Design interfaces that can handle large amounts of data (lists, contract clauses, metadata) without overwhelming the user. You know when to use a table, when to use a card, and how to manage whitespace in a data-heavy B2B environment.

• Error Prevention: Design "guardrails" that prevent non-technical users from making critical errors in the administration process.

Design System & Engineering Collaboration

• Shadcn & Tailwind Implementation: You won't be building a design system from scratch. You will leverage and theme Shadcn UI components and Tailwind CSS . Your job is to apply these constraints creatively to build consistent, developer-friendly designs.

• Developer Hand-off: Work closely with frontend engineers. You understand the "box model" and can design in Figma with auto-layout in a way that translates 1:1 to React components.

• Design QA : Partner with Engineering during implementation to ensure the shipped experience matches design intent, resolving UX edge cases within technical constraints.

Research & Empathy

• User Advocacy: Our users are cross-functional teams, from sales agents and administrators to project stakeholders and executives. They are time-constrained, context-switch constantly, and need to move work forward with minimal training. You will conduct research to understand how each group organizes information, makes decisions, and completes key workflows, then map the UI to match that reality and reduce cognitive load.

• Legacy Migration: Help users transition from the legacy platform to the new system. Identify which workflows are must-haves versus clutter, then design the bridge to the new experience with clear patterns and minimal disruption.

Who You Are

• The Simplifier: You look at a screen with 50 inputs and instinctively know how to group, paginate, or progressively disclose them to make it approachable.

• The Component thinker: You don't just draw rectangles; you think in atoms, molecules, and organisms. You understand how a change to a button in the library affects the whole platform.

• The Pragmatist: You understand the balance between "pixel perfect" and "shipping value." You are comfortable using an existing library (Shadcn) to speed up development rather than reinventing standard patterns.

Qualifications

• Experience: 5+ years of Product Design experience, specifically in B2B SaaS or complex enterprise tools.

• Portfolio: Must show examples of workflow design , data tables, dashboards, or form-heavy interfaces.

• Technical Fluency: Strong familiarity with Atomic Design principles and experience designing for React/Tailwind environments. You don't need to code, but you need to know how the code works.

• Domain Experience: Experience in PropTech, LegalTech, HR Tech, ERPs, or Document Management systems is a massive plus.

Tech Stack Context for the Designer

• Design Tool: Figma (Auto-layout mastery required)

• Frontend Framework: React

• Styling/UI Library: Tailwind CSS / Shadcn UI

Please note: this is a fully remote, work-from-home position.

The Role

We're hiring a UI Product Designer to own how Proton looks and works. Reporting to the VP of Product, you'll ship in a squad with PMs and engineers, and you'll be in front of customers constantly, watching reps use what you built and bringing back what you can only learn in person. Our product people know their users by name, not through a research summary.

Those users sit in one screen for eight hours a day and have spent their careers with software they merely tolerate. We want them to have something they'd choose: fast, modern, a pleasure to use. That's the hard version of the job, because most of the UI patterns you'd reach for by default were drawn for software that couldn't think. Ours can.

Two things make this role different from a standard product design opening:

• You're an AI-native designer, not just a Figma operator. Everyone here uses Claude Code and similar agentic tools as a first-class collaborator. We expect concepts prototyped in real code, put in front of people, and iterated with heavy AI leverage. Prototype before you polish, and make the calls AI can't.

• You set the craft bar. This hire decides how Proton looks and feels. Distribution software is famously grim and we intend to be the exception. You'll own the visual language and the design system across all four products.

Location : Cambridge, MA (hybrid, 3 days a week in Harvard Square) or remote in the EU.

Level : Product Designer through Senior Product Designer. Scope and autonomy change across that range.

Compensation : $80k – $100k base depending on experience, plus bonus, equity, and full benefits. EU offers are benchmarked to local market.

What You'll Do

• Prototype in code with Claude Code or Cursor to feel an interaction before we commit

• Own the design system: components, interactions, documentation, and the harder part, getting every squad to use them.

• Define what AI looks like here. Nobody has settled patterns yet, so you'll decide what it looks like when a rep trusts an agent and when they overrule one.

• Work inside our agentic scrum model. We don't run two-week sprints; cadence follows what a team and its agents can ship, and you'll help work out what design looks like in that.

• Get in front of customers constantly, including onsite. Distributors work in warehouses and on sales floors, and the best design calls come from standing next to a rep.

Requirements

• Craft that is demonstrably yours. Command of typography, layout, color, hierarchy, and iconography, with motion when it earns its place. You pull references from well outside software, and your work looks like someone made it rather than assembled it. We are explicitly not hiring people who let AI make their taste decisions. AI amplifies taste, it doesn't create it.

• Real end-to-end delivery. Shipped products, real users, real ownership, alongside PM and engineering. Hands-on work, not an LLM-generated portfolio.

• Daily, hands-on use of AI in your practice. Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent, used to ship real work rather than generate comps. You can say concretely how you structure context and check what comes back.

• A portfolio. Products or features you took from concept to launch where you set the visual language yourself. We're most interested in a workflow you found trapped in a legacy system and reimagined: what you kept, what you threw out, and how you got people to move.

• Systems thinking. You can author one beautiful screen and write the rules that let others make fifty consistent ones. You are curious enough to understand what's cheap to build and what isn't.

• Real agile experience, and a pull toward customers. You've worked inside traditional scrum and know what those rituals were for. We've replaced it with an agentic scrum, and knowing the original is what lets you help rebuild it. You'd also rather be in the room with a user than briefed about them.

Big Plus

• Complex B2B, enterprise, or ERP-adjacent software, with high-frequency users and workflows people can't opt out of.

• Agentic products, and the patterns for trust, correction, and handoff between a person and an agent.

• Early-stage SaaS startups.

• Flexible schedule with high autonomy.

• Unlimited PTO + 10 company-paid holidays.

• 12 weeks fully paid parental leave (primary and secondary, including adoption and fostering).

• Annual company-paid offsites.

Who are we looking for

Perfect for a senior who wants to think as part of the job (not just ship).

On Kota Embed you design a surface where a sort-order decision moves real money for tens of thousands of people, where the data model is co-designed with the UI, where 6–10 stakeholders are co-present in major decisions, where constraints become design surfaces rather than obstacles, where prototypes are spec, and where the work compounds into a body of named, citable patterns rather than dissolving into ad-hoc Figma files.

At this moment this is not a steady-state senior IC role. It's a "the ground is moving and you need to own the design quality while it does" role.

You need to want that, not just tolerate it.

What we are looking for

•
A designer who has worked inside a complex product (ideally B2B, double ideally it was API-driven), understands why the data model constrains the interface, and finds that constraint interesting rather than annoying.

•
You've shipped something with invisible complexity. Not a marketing site, not a dashboard with toggles. You succeeded, and you can explain how you thought through it.

•
Research methods at sprint cadence. 5-user tests, rapid Figma Make/Cursor/Paper prototyping, Datadog/Mixpanel log analysis, facilitating internal design reviews. You also know when to skip research and ship. The mantra: "rough data is better than no data; you can't remove uncertainty - triage it"

•
Outcomes-over-outputs discipline. Lock down problem / assumptions / success criteria before agreeing to a solution.

•
Systems thinking - promoting patterns to primitives. Recurring interaction surfaces become design-system components.

•
UX influence work. Getting devs/stakeholders to attend usability sessions. Building and facilitating ceremonies (standups, retros, backlog grooming) so design becomes shared team context, not an isolated artifact.

•
Craft fundamentals. Type, spacing, rhythm, hierarchy. The basics, worked at 400% zoom - quality and speed aren't opposites.

•
Builder craft. Cursor / Claude Code comfort. Treating prototypes as spec means producing working prototypes is the design output. Closing the gap between design and engineering rather than widening it.

Things you might know about or be interested in

•
Embedded financial products.

•
Fintech, financial services, insurance, or benefits platforms.

•
Developer product experiences, understanding of how to design for technical users and embedded/integration-heavy products.

Our values

•
Have Integrity. We care deeply about our why and it won’t jeopardise our how.

•
Care Deeply. Our products are our story, we look at the details, go the extra mile to delight customers.

•
Own Your Ship . Ask why, do the work, get the data, solve the problem, be an owner.

•
Raise the Bar . We continuously look to push past good enough. Expect more, move faster, and never stop raising your and the team’s standards.

•
Play to Win . We exist because we decided to say no to the norm – now we do this everyday.

Annual, company-wide offsite

Summary of the Role:

As a Product Designer at Maze, you'll define what product design looks like for AI agents in cybersecurity — a problem space where the design patterns don't exist yet. This is an early-hire role at a well-funded Series A startup building at the intersection of generative AI and security, and you'll own the product surface end-to-end while working directly with our Head of Product, engineering, and founders.

The product challenge is genuinely new. Our AI agents investigate vulnerabilities autonomously, surface findings with real context, and collaborate with security teams to cut through noise. Your job is to design how humans and agents work together — how trust gets built, how decisions get communicated, how complex security workflows become understandable. There's no playbook for this. You'll create one.

This role suits someone who operates closer to a product director than a screen-shipper — driving direction, influencing strategy, and making business-impact calls, alongside the visual craft to deliver them. You'll be using AI tools daily to move faster, but your craft is the floor: every design choice should hold up on its own merits, independent of how it was generated. Success looks like a design system shipped and adopted across the product, and concrete product outcomes — feature adoption, POC-to-customer conversion, and customer satisfaction with the experiences you ship.

Your Contribution:

•
Define AI-Agent UX Patterns: Design how security teams collaborate with autonomous AI agents — how investigations get presented, how trust is established, how humans steer the agent without slowing it down. You're inventing patterns, not applying existing ones.

•
Drive Product Direction, Not Just Design: Operate as a product-led designer — shaping roadmap, challenging requirements, influencing leadership with research and business reasoning. The bar is "what should we build, and why" alongside "how should it look."

•
Own the Product Surface End-to-End: Take features from problem framing through shipped product, working in tight partnership with PMs and engineers — including backend. Run discovery, prototype rapidly, validate with customers, and stay close to implementation. No throwing designs over the wall, no shipping around the engineering team.

•
Build the Design System: Create and scale a component-based design system that becomes the foundation for everything we ship. Establish patterns for AI-human collaboration that the team can build on as we grow.

•
Pioneer AI-Assisted Design Workflows: Use AI tools to accelerate ideation, prototyping, and exploration — and develop the methodologies the rest of the team will adopt. Your daily workflow is itself a contribution.

•
Translate Research Into Design: Run customer research, talk to security teams directly, and turn what you learn into shipped product. Use AI-assisted analysis to move from insight to prototype in days, not weeks.

•
Set the Quality Bar: Establish what "good" looks like for product design at Maze across craft, consistency, and customer impact — as the foundation for a design team that scales behind you.

What You Need to Be Successful:

•
Visual Craft for Data-Dense UI: A portfolio that holds up to detailed scrutiny — strong colour theory, deliberate visual hierarchy, considered information architecture for complex workflows. This is the bar, not a nice-to-have. Your interview will dig into specific design choices and why you made them.

•
Product Design Track Record: 4-7 years of professional product design experience, with shipped work in B2B SaaS. We're flexible on years; demonstrated craft and clear ownership matter more than time served.

•
Data-Heavy B2B Interfaces: Direct experience designing for complex workflows, dense data, and technical audiences. Dashboards, investigation tools, developer products, security platforms — the kind of UI where information density and decision support actually matter.

AI as Tool, Not Crutch: You use AI tools (Figma AI, Cursor, v0, Midjourney, ChatGPT/Claude, etc.) as part of your daily workflow and can speak credibly to what they're good for and where they break down.
